All five below oEmbed-verified 2026-08-07; facts sourced from data/junior-career.json (two-source verified) — do not add a detail here that the dataset does not carry.

moments.title: The debut
moments.text: Sixteenth on the grid, rain falling, 18 years old. He crosses the line fourth — the second-youngest points scorer in Formula 1 history, behind only Max Verstappen. A penalty briefly demotes him; Mercedes gets it overturned on review.
moments.videoTitle: Race Highlights | 2025 Australian Grand Prix — FORMULA 1

moments.title: The record pole
moments.text: Sprint qualifying, sixth Grand Prix weekend of his career. Pole position at 18 years, 8 months and 7 days — the youngest polesitter in any Formula 1 qualifying format, breaking a Sebastian Vettel record that had stood since 2008. By more than two years.
moments.videoTitle: Sprint Qualifying Highlights | 2025 Miami Grand Prix — FORMULA 1

moments.title: The first podium
moments.text: Third place in Montreal at 18 years and 294 days, behind race-winner teammate Russell — the first Italian on a Formula 1 podium since Jarno Trulli in 2009. Then he flew home to Bologna and sat his high-school final exams. Passed those too.
moments.videoTitle: Race Highlights | 2025 Canadian Grand Prix — FORMULA 1

moments.title: The maiden win
moments.text: First Grand Prix pole, converted into a first Grand Prix win — the youngest Grand Prix polesitter in F1 history, only the second teenager ever to win a Grand Prix after Verstappen, and the first Italian to win a Formula 1 race in twenty years. Fisichella, Malaysia 2006, was the last.
moments.videoTitle: Race Highlights | 2026 Chinese Grand Prix — FORMULA 1

moments.title: The grand chelem
moments.text: Pole. Victory. Every lap led. Fastest lap. At 19, the youngest driver ever to take a grand chelem — and the youngest winner Monaco has ever crowned. His fifth consecutive victory, in the race every driver grows up dreaming about.
moments.videoTitle: Race Highlights | 2026 Monaco Grand Prix — FORMULA 1
